subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw core expose model-callable cross-gateway session routing through `gateway.peers` or raw `gatewayUrl`, or should this PR pause until a federation/peer-auth contract is approved?
rationale: The requested workflow is real, but the implementation changes gateway trust boundaries, session ownership, message delivery, config surface, and model-visible remote routing policy.

options.title: Pause for a federation contract
options.body: Require maintainer-approved peer identity, URL allowlist, scopes, idempotency/replay, and session visibility semantics before this core surface lands.

options.title: Narrow to configured peers only
options.body: Remove raw `gatewayUrl` from session tools and allow only explicitly configured peers after a security review and live upgrade proof.

options.title: Accept experimental core routing
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally accept the wider trust boundary, but should do so with documented risk and required live multi-gateway proof.

recommendation.title: Pause for a federation contract
recommendation.body: Require maintainer-approved peer identity, URL allowlist, scopes, idempotency/replay, and session visibility semantics before this core surface lands.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal ties this decision to session-tool architecture and gatewayUrl security hardening.
